```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(mgcv)
library(modelr)
library(p8105.datasets)

set.seed(1)
```

```{r}
n_samp = 250

sim_df_const = 
  tibble(
    x = rnorm(n_samp, 1, 1),
    error = rnorm(n_samp, 0, 1),
    y = 2 + 3 * x + error
  )

sim_df_const |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()
```

```{r}
sim_df_nonconst = 
  sim_df_const |> 
  mutate(
    error = error * .75 * x, #outcome variance depends on the predictor now (because x). this leads to nonconstant variance
    y = 2 + 3 * x + error 
  )

sim_df_nonconst |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") #CI should be much bigger at tails where there is large variance - fix this 
```

Fix the regressions 

```{r}
sim_df_const |> 
  lm(y ~ x, data = _) |> 
  broom::tidy() |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Nonconstant 

```{r}
sim_df_nonconst |> 
  lm(y ~ x, data = _) |> 
  broom::tidy() |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
Let's try to get a CI for this dataset that we trust a bit more. 

#Draw a bootstrap sample 

Let's always write a little function 

```{r}
draw_boot_sample = function(df) {
  
  sample_frac(df, replace = TRUE)
  
}
```

Does this work?

```{r}
sim_df_nonconst |> 
  draw_boot_sample() |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```
Re-running --> slightly different datasets each time 
Generate 1000 bootstrap samples and 1000 regressions and take the results 

Draw a bunch of samples and analyze 

```{r}
boot_straps = 
  tibble(
    strap_number = 1:1000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    strap_sample = map(strap_number, \(i) draw_boot_sample (sim_df_nonconst))
  )
```

```{r}
boot_strap_df = 
  tibble(
    strap_number = 1:1000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    strap_sample = map(strap_number, \(i) draw_boot_sample (sim_df_nonconst)), 
    model_fit = map(strap_sample, \(df) lm(y ~ x, data = df)), 
    results = map(model_fit, broom::tidy)
  ) 
```

Did this work?

```{r}
boot_strap_df |> 
  select(strap_number, results) |> 
  unnest(results) |> 
  group_by(term) |> 
  summarize(
    mean_est = mean(estimate), 
    se_est = sd(estimate)
  )
```
Estimates are about the same as OG dataset, but SE is different (bigger for slope, lower for intercept) 

Look at the results more 

```{r}
boot_strap_df |> 
  select(strap_number, strap_sample) |> 
  unnest(strap_sample) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, group = strap_number)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, alpha = .3) +
  geom_point(data = sim_df_nonconst, aes(group = NULL), alpha = .6)
```

Quick notes

```{r}
boot_straps = 
  sim_df_nonconst |> 
  modelr::bootstrap(n = 1000)
```

What about bootstrapping in a dataset when we trust the assumptions? 
```{r}
boot_strap_df_constant = 
  tibble(
    strap_number = 1:1000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    strap_sample = map(strap_number, \(i) draw_boot_sample (sim_df_const)), 
    model_fit = map(strap_sample, \(df) lm(y ~ x, data = df)), 
    results = map(model_fit, broom::tidy)
  ) 
```
This gives you the same assumptions as the OG dataset (which is good because we trust those assumptions!) - it will give you the right answer 

## Airbnb 

```{r}
data("nyc_airbnb")

nyc_airbnb = 
  nyc_airbnb |> 
  mutate(
    stars = review_scores_location / 2
  ) |> 
  rename(
    borough = neighbourhood_group, 
    neighborhood = neighbourhood
  ) |> 
  filter(borough != "Staten Island") |> 
  drop_na(price, stars) |> 
  select(price, stars, borough, neighborhood, room_type)
```

this doesn't look good: 
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = stars, y = price, color = room_type)) +
  geom_point()
```
Skewed data, if we fit a linear regression model to this, I dont know if I'd trust it 

Bootstrap

```{r}
airbnb_bootstrap_df = 
  nyc_airbnb |> 
  filter(borough == "Manhattan") |> 
  modelr::bootstrap(n = 1000) |> 
  mutate( #jumping to results 
    model_fits = map(strap, \(df) lm (price ~ stars + room_type, data = df)), 
    results = map(model_fits, broom::tidy)
  )
```

are these coefficients close enough to normal that I can trust default inference? 

```{r}
airbnb_bootstrap_df |> 
  select(results) |> 
  unnest(results)
```

```{r}
airbnb_bootstrap_df |> 
  select(results) |> 
  unnest(results) |> 
  filter(term == "stars") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate)) + 
  geom_density()
```
Does not look super symmetric 

CI for stars slope: 

```{r}
airbnb_bootstrap_df |> 
  select(results) |> 
  unnest(results) |> 
  filter(term == "stars") |> 
  summarize(
    slope_estimate = mean(estimate), 
    ci_lb = quantile(estimate, 0.025),
    ci_ub = quantile(estimate, 0.975)
  )
```

# LIDAR

```{r}
data("lidar")

lidar |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = range, y = logratio)) + 
  geom_point() + 
    stat_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x))
```

```{r}
lidar |> 
  modelr::bootstrap(n = 250) |> 
  mutate(
    models = map(strap, \(df) gam(logratio ~ s(range), data = df)),
    results = map(models, \(mod) modelr::add_predictions(data = lidar, model = mod))) |> 
  select(.id, results) |> 
  unnest(results) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = range, y = pred, group = .id)) + 
  geom_path(color = "blue", alpha = .5) + 
  geom_point(data = lidar, aes(y = logratio, group = NULL))
```
